question: Across millions of research papers since the 1950s, which more often became highly cited: solo work or team work?
answer: Papers by teams. Wuchty, Jones and Uzzi analysed nearly 20 million papers and 2 million patents over five decades: teams came to dominate, and team papers were more likely to become very highly cited, an edge that grew over time. The lone genius makes the better story; the group in the lab does most of the work.
move: A story needs one hero; real results usually need a team.
ask: Whose quiet help is missing from the story I tell about my own successes?
trap: Breakthrough stories feature a lone genius, so solo papers should stand out.
reference: Stefan Wuchty, Benjamin F. Jones and Brian Uzzi, The Increasing Dominance of Teams in Production of Knowledge, Science, 2007
